SATURDAY'S RUN NEVER GOT A RECAP, SO IT GETS ONE HERE. This loop did not run Saturday evening — the newest outbox on disk before tonight was Friday's — and 8.72 km has been sitting unanalysed since. 07:08 start, 45:25 of moving time, 8.72 km, 5:12 per kilometre on average, average heart rate 141 against a peak of 181, load 53, and you rated it a 6.

Nine were in the Zone X band between 4:42 and 5:01 — the one worth staying out of. Just over two minutes were at Zone 3 pace or faster, and that is where the 181 comes from: one short surge, a hill or a finish rather than a decision. The rep-by-rep pass was refused, and correctly. deepdive.py ran on it at 19:44 and returned valid:false because the activity is named San Francisco rather than an 80/20 code, so there is no published structure to window the trace against — and it will not interpolate one from a name. recap.takeaways:
1) WEEK 16 OPENS TOMORROW MORNING AND THERE IS STILL NO PLAN FILE — and tonight I can tell you exactly what will stop it, which is worth more than saying it a fourth time. WEEK_14_PLAN.md is still the newest plan on disk and the plan-gen heartbeat still reads 7 September, unchanged as of 19:45 tonight. Read fresh off the grid, week 16 is CF3, CT31 and CFF18 on the bike and RAn3 and RT19 on the run — 8:39 at 81/19, the deload, carrying both block-boundary retests. I checked all five against 80_20_WORKOUT_DEFINITIONS.md: CF3, CT31, RAn3 and RT19 are cached with verified structures. CFF18 is not. Only CFF16 is, at 150 minutes, and the trailing number does not track duration in that family, so nothing can be inferred from the neighbour. That one missing structure is precisely what stopped plan-gen on 6 September. Pull CFF18 from the live library first and the rest of week 16 writes itself.

2) THE ANCHORS ARE THE WHOLE POINT OF WEEK 16, AND THEY ARE SEVEN WEEKS OLD. FTP 236 W, bike LTHR 159, run threshold 4:22 per kilometre, run LTHR 167 — all written by tune.py on 28 and 30 July and untouched since, with two scheduled retests lost in between. Every band on the Programme tab, every zone I just judged Saturday's run against, and every target in whatever week 17 becomes all rest on those four numbers. A lost week of base costs a week. A lost retest costs the accuracy of everything prescribed after it.

3) AND YOU ARE IN THE BEST STATE TO TEST IN THAT YOU HAVE BEEN IN A MONTH — the one genuinely good thing about how this week went. Off today's wellness row: fitness 41.9, fatigue 37.8, form +4.1. Two weeks ago, on 6 September, the same three read 50.7, 63.9 and −13.2. Fitness is down nine points; fatigue is down twenty-six. Recovered and under-stimulated at the same time — the wrong way to arrive at a retest week and the right condition to walk into one with. Saturday's call was the right one, and it is worth saying so plainly: you kept it long and easy with nothing on any page asking you to.

4) ADAPT: NO-OP, by necessity rather than judgement. Classifying today as executed, modified, failed or skipped needs a prescription to classify it against, and there is none — no plan file for the week and zero planned events on intervals for 14–20 September. No plan file edited, no future day row changed, no expected figure touched. Two mechanical notes for the morning watchdog: today's dashboard refresh did not run, so dashboard-data.json still carries yesterday's date and github-deploy has skipped three publish attempts tonight on exactly that, which means this recap reaches the phone whenever the next refresh writes; and the machine appears to have been off until 19:44, which is why tonight's fetch is an hour and a quarter later than its 18:30 slot rather than early.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.

Your own note, logged last night: you rotated the week rather than dropping a session — CF3 done Monday, CT31 to Tuesday, RAn3 out to Friday. Intervals already carries it that way. Sunday's plan licensed you to move the retest AND spend RAn3; you took the first half and refused the second, and that is the better version of the rule. THE NUMBERS. Sleeping heart rate came in at 67 bpm against a 63 bpm sixty-night baseline — twelve beats better than yesterday morning and the closest to your own normal since 10 September. You slept 8.1 hours with nine minutes awake and 62 minutes of deep sleep, the best night on file in twelve days. Wrist temperature is 36.33 °C, down from 36.64 but still 0.42 above baseline, so readiness.py's illness flag stays up for a second morning. Breathing is 13.4, on the good side of baseline. Readiness prints 37, Ease off. WHICH I WEIGHT AND WHY, AND WHERE THE NUMBER IS MISLEADING YOU: 37 is dragged almost entirely by the heart-rate term, and that term smooths the last three ROWS in the file — 16, 21 and 22 September — which are eleven days apart, so it is still carrying the 82 bpm travel night from nearly a week ago. The single new night is genuinely good. I weight last night over the smoothed index, and I weight the temperature against it, because two mornings of elevated skin temperature is the one signal here that has not turned. THE CALL: RIDE IT, and ride it indoors on Zwift with power. Not because the flag has cleared, but because CT31 has nowhere else to go — Wednesday is class-only travel, Thursday is nothing, Friday now carries RAn3 on front-squat legs, Saturday is the 150-minute ride with the reference block and Sunday is the run retest. Move it twice and it does not happen, and the anchors stay 54 days old. THE GATE IS THE SAME ONE AS YESTERDAY AND IT IS REAL: 5 minutes Zone 1, then 15 minutes Zone 2 at 165–196 W. If that stretch feels like work rather than like settling in, stop there and take the spin — CT31 then rolls to Monday of week 13R and nothing is lost but a week.
